channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: “O governo brasileiro não vacilará” na defesa da soberania, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula stated that Brazil will not waver in defending national sovereignty, in response to the new 25% tariff imposed by the U.S. on Brazilian imports. The comment was made in an Instagram post, emphasizing that protecting sovereignty is an obligation above all interests. The Brazilian government is seeking to respond firmly to U.S. trade measures.

item.title: Tarifaço deve impactar 18% das exportações para os EUA, estima governo
item.description: U.S. tariffs are expected to directly impact 2,400 Brazilian companies accounting for 18% of Brazil’s exports to the United States, valued at $7.4 billion. The most affected sectors include wood, machinery, furniture, ceramics, footwear, and sugar, while meats and coffee were largely spared. The government says it will continue pursuing market diversification, as the U.S. share of Brazilian exports fell from 12.1% to 9.4% in 2026.

item.title: Renan Santos anuncia show de rock gratuito após cancelamento no Rio
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Renan Santos (Missão) announced a free rock concert by his band, Banda Limão Rosa, at Bar Bukowski in Rio de Janeiro, following the cancellation of a show at Audio Rebel due to pressure from left-wing activists. He denounced the cancellation as authoritarian and ridiculous, insisting the band performs only existential and relationship-themed music, not political acts. The new show will be free, in a larger venue, and he expects a full house.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que defender mulher de covarde e vagabundo é pauta da direita
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, announced he will create the 'Central da Mulher', a public security platform focused on women, if elected. He stated that defending women from cowards and vagabonds is a typical right-wing agenda.

item.title: Flávio volta a defender mulher como vice e cita Daniella Marques, Simone Marchetto e Clarissa Tércio
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) reiterated his preference for a female running mate in his 2026 presidential ticket, naming Daniella Marques, Simone Marchetto, and Clarissa Tércio as potential candidates. He also launched the 'Brasil por Elas' program, featuring job apps, childcare vouchers, microcredit for women entrepreneurs, and chemical castration for rapists, while criticizing President Lula for not using a cellphone, calling it emblematic of an analog and disconnected government.

item.title: A reação do governo Lula ao novo tarifaço de Trump: 'Seguiremos sem viralatice'
item.description: The Lula government reacted to the 25% US tariffs on Brazilian goods by calling it political interference and announcing the activation of the Reciprocity Law, while remaining open to negotiations. Ministers, including Vice President Alckmin and Finance Minister Durigan, rebuked Marco Rubio's accusations and refused to act with 'viralatice'.

item.title: Após crise com Michelle, Flávio Bolsonaro anuncia plano de governo voltado às mulheres com plataforma digital e IA própria
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro announced the 'Brasil Por Elas' program targeting women, featuring internet access for 70 million, an AI named Maria, and the 'Central da Mulher' digital platform, following his estrangement from Michelle Bolsonaro. The plan includes eliminating daycare queues, providing vouchers for mothers without childcare access, expanding elderly care, and promoting female entrepreneurship. Danielle Marques, former Caixa president and potential finance minister, participated in the announcement and made controversial remarks about the left.

item.title: Lula faz do limão uma limonada e é o único a ganhar com o tarifaço dos EUA, mais um erro de Flávio
item.description: The U.S. imposed a politically motivated tariff based on false data to favor Brazil’s right-wing, but the move backfired and ultimately benefited Lula, who regained popular approval. Flávio Bolsonaro made a strategic error by supporting the tariff and Marco Rubio, aligning with the aggressor instead of defending Brazil, triggering strong backlash and the viral term 'Tariflávio' on social media. Despite intensive Brazilian diplomatic efforts, the U.S. decision was pre-made, and Flávio failed to mitigate the damage, while Lula strengthened his position.

item.title: TSE inicia articulação com emissoras para criação de pool de mídia das Eleições 2026
item.description: The TSE began discussions with radio and TV broadcasters to create a media pool to support free political advertising in the 2026 General Elections, with free airtime scheduled from August 28 to October 1, 2026. The initiative aims to ensure greater transmission security, faster compliance with judicial rulings, and more efficient distribution of party materials, as stated by Audit Secretary Carlos Ramon.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro precisa explicar o uso do dinheiro de Vorcaro, não a foto com ‘Sicário’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) has not provided an account of the use of US$10 million received from banker Daniel Vorcaro to finance a film about his father, Jair Bolsonaro, despite promising to do so within 30 days starting May 19. The deadline expired on June 19, and as of today, no financial report has been submitted, which commentator Carlos Andreazza identifies as the real issue — not the photo with the alleged 'Sicario,' but the lack of transparency regarding the funds received.

item.title: Tarifaço: Lula diz que Brasil "não vacilará" na defesa da soberania
item.description: President Lula declared Brazil will not falter in defending its sovereignty following the U.S. announcement of a 25% additional tariff on Brazilian exports, effective July 22. The measure, based on Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, targets industrial goods, consumer products, and certain commodities, while exempting items like coffee, açaí, and beef. Lula emphasized that safeguarding national sovereignty is a duty above all political parties and trends.

item.title: 'Defender mulher é pauta de direita', diz Flávio Bolsonaro ao anunciar propostas para mulheres
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro asserted that defending women is a right-wing agenda, claiming 'those who like criminals are on the left,' while launching the 'Brasil por Elas' plan with proposals including expanded internet access, a 'Women's Center' for protection and support, vouchers for childcare and rent, an AI assistant named 'Maria,' and unified health records. He positioned Caixa Econômica Federal as a tool for women's financial autonomy, aiming to repair his standing with female voters after public disputes with Michelle Bolsonaro.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que foto com 'Sicário' de Vorcaro é manipulação de IA
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) claimed that a photo showing him alongside Luiz Phillipi Machado de Moraes Mourão, known as the 'Sicário' of Daniel Vorcaro, is an AI manipulation, alleging the editors forgot to remove an exaggeratedly large finger. The image, published by ICL and fact-checked by g1, shows low probability of AI manipulation, and the senator’s press office denies any knowledge of the person in the photo. Mourão was identified by the Federal Police as a coordinator of a private militia linked to Vorcaro and arrested in March 2026.

item.title: PIX, STF, redes sociais: governo Lula contesta argumentos dos EUA para novo tarifaço contra o Brasil
item.description: The Lula government contests the 25% tariffs imposed by the U.S., arguing that the justifications—based on PIX, STF actions against big techs, corruption, and deforestation—are unfounded and protectionist. Brazil asserts that PIX expanded financial inclusion and that credit card usage grew 150% since its launch, while also becoming a global reference in instant payment systems. The government announced it will immediately initiate procedures under the Reciprocity Law in response to the tariff measure.

item.title: A resposta de Messi a insinuações sobre favorecimento da Argentina na Copa do Mundo
item.description: Lionel Messi responded to allegations of favorable refereeing for Argentina in the 2026 World Cup, stating the team earned the title through consistent performance over the last four years. He emphasized that reaching two consecutive finals is a rare achievement and that the victory over England was not due to luck but skill and effort. Controversies include complaints from Switzerland and Egypt over disputed decisions in the round of 16 and quarterfinals, respectively.

item.title: The Guardian: Trump trata soberania do Brasil como “prática desleal”
item.description: The Guardian criticizes the Trump administration for framing Brazil’s sovereign decisions—such as the Pix payment system and a Supreme Court ruling increasing platform liability for hate speech—as unfair trade practices to justify a new 25% tariff on Brazilian goods. The tariff, announced the day after the editorial, takes effect on July 22 with exemptions for items like coffee, beef, and orange juice. The article links the U.S. stance to corporate interests harmed by Brazil’s regulatory autonomy, particularly in finance and tech.

item.title: Renan faz críticas a Lula e Flávio após tarifaço
item.description: Renan Santos, pre-candidate of the Missão party for the presidency, harshly criticized President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for their stance on the U.S.-imposed tariff surge, accusing Lula of lacking the ability to negotiate rare earths and the Bolsonaro family of being a "lackey" of the U.S. government.

item.title: Rollemberg usa painel para disseminar propaganda; conduta é vedada
item.description: An electronic billboard displaying propaganda for pre-candidate Rodrigo Rollemberg (PSB-DF) was spotted in Brasília’s Cruzeiro region, violating electoral law that bans outdoor political advertising, even without an explicit call to vote. The ad highlights Rollemberg’s positions on issues such as the 6×1 work schedule and parliamentary amendment allocations. Rollemberg has not commented, and electoral authorities may order the removal of the billboard and impose a fine.

item.title: TSE firma cooperação com big techs e empresas de IA para prevenir riscos nas eleições
item.description: The president of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), Kássio Nunes Marques, met with representatives of major tech companies and AI firms to establish cooperation agreements aimed at preventing risks in the 2026 elections. The initiative seeks to combat disinformation, content manipulation, and misuse of technology in the electoral process. The partnership underscores the TSE’s commitment to safeguarding electoral integrity through technological collaboration.

item.title: Veículos de comunicação têm até segunda (20) para informar à JE dados de representantes legais
item.description: Communication vehicles, including radio and TV broadcasters, internet application providers, and other media companies, must submit to the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) by next Monday (20) the details of their legal representatives, correspondence addresses, email, and mobile phone numbers with instant messaging apps. The requirement applies without prior notice and is based on Articles 10 of TSE Resolution No. 23,608/2019 and 79 of TSE Resolution No. 23,610/2019. It is also possible to designate a prosecutor with or without authority to receive citations, provided the corresponding power of attorney is submitted.

item.title: Renan Santos (Missão) ataca Lula e Flávio por tarifaço e diz que negociaria terras raras
item.description: Renan Santos, pré-candidate of the Missão party for presidency, accused President Lula (PT) of 'pushing the issue with his belly' regarding the 25% tariff imposed by the U.S. on Brazilian products, calling the government's stance passive. He also criticized Flávio Bolsonaro as 'incompetent' in U.S. negotiations, stating that under his leadership, he would directly negotiate rare earth trade terms to prevent such protectionist measures.

item.title: Bolsonaristas extremistas jogam contra o Brasil
item.description: The report claims that members of the Bolsonaro family, especially Eduardo Bolsonaro, who lives in the U.S., collaborated with the American government to impose tariffs on Brazil to harm the economy and shift voter perception against Flávio Bolsonaro. This action is described as undemocratic and treasonous, as it allegedly used a foreign government to attack an elected president and the nation, regardless of views on Lula. The text condemns this conduct as opportunistic and extremist, incompatible with democratic values.

item.title: Em reunião com big techs, Nunes Marques fala em criar governança para antecipar riscos e alerta sobre IA generativa
item.description: TSE President Minister Nunes Marques announced in a meeting with big tech representatives — including Meta, Google, TikTok, and X — the signing of a memorandum of understanding to establish shared governance against disinformation and generative AI, including voice-cloning prevention technology with ElevenLabs. Although a draft regulation on platform compliance plans was not discussed, companies approached the minister afterward to suggest adjustments, highlighting efforts to balance regulation with corporate autonomy.

item.title: Incômodo dos EUA é por Brasil “não ter se curvado”, diz Mauro Vieira
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira accused the U.S. of imposing a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods as retaliation for Brazil’s refusal to yield to what he called unreasonable and excessive demands during negotiations. He described the measure as politically motivated, lacking legal basis, and announced after over 30 bilateral meetings, including 11 contacts with senior U.S. officials, without any reciprocal concessions offered to Brazil.

item.title: TSE firma parceria com big techs para combater desinformação na eleição
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has formalized partnerships with major technology companies including TikTok, Facebook, WhatsApp, Telegram, LinkedIn, Google, Instagram, X, Kwai, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, and Anthropic to combat disinformation in the 2026 elections. The agreements include commitments integrated into the Permanent Program to Counter Disinformation, aiming to promote reliable information, restrict AI voice cloning, and enable autonomous removal of misleading content. This initiative builds on TSE resolutions from March 2026 that ban AI-generated content imitating candidates in the 72 hours before and 24 hours after voting, requiring clear labeling and immediate takedown of manipulated media.

item.title: Eleições 2026: TSE e plataformas digitais firmam parcerias para ampliar combate à desinformação
item.description: TSE President Minister Kassio Nunes Marques signed memorandums of understanding with major digital platforms operating in Brazil to strengthen the fight against disinformation in the 2026 elections. The partnerships aim to enhance technical cooperation to detect and reduce false narratives about electronic voting machines and the voting system, with special attention to the improper use of artificial intelligence. The minister emphasized that the 2026 elections will be the most digitized in the country’s history, requiring improved mechanisms to control the flow of information.

item.title: Líder do PL no Senado diz não ter "rabo preso": "Tenho CPF próprio"
item.description: Senate Liberal Party leader Carlos Portinho (PL-RJ) says he has no 'skeletons in the closet' to run for re-election as senator from Rio de Janeiro, emphasizing his clean record, 25 years in public office, and personal CPF. He was named the PL’s pre-candidate after Cláudio Castro stepped down due to PF investigations and Márcio Canella was arrested on weapons charges, both linked to PF operations, clearing the way for his candidacy.

item.title: Lula buscou diálogo com Trump e quer seguir negociando, diz Vieira
item.description: Chancellor Mauro Vieira stated that President Lula sought dialogue with the U.S. to avoid new tariffs, emphasizing Brazil's willingness to negotiate. Despite this, data shows Lula criticized Trump in 62 instances since 2023, while Trump mentioned Lula only 11 times since January 2025. Vieira also condemned Secretary of State Marco Rubio for 'rude and arrogant' remarks against Lula, claiming the U.S. tariffs lack justification and are politically motivated.

item.title: TSE firma cooperação com big techs e empresas de IA para prevenir riscos à integridade das eleições
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques met with representatives from seven major tech platforms (Kwai, Telegram, Meta, TikTok, Google, X, and LinkedIn) and three AI companies (ElevenLabs, OpenAI, and Anthropic) to sign memoranda of understanding aimed at combating disinformation and fake profiles in the 2026 elections. Microsoft is expected to formalize its partnership in the coming days. The TSE emphasized that the cooperation seeks to ensure access to reliable information and reduce electoral fraud, without restricting freedom of expression or imposing an official narrative on political debate.

item.title: Líderes de Lula no Congresso se unem para atrelar Flávio ao tarifaço
item.description: Lula’s congressional leaders claim the new 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods are a political move designed to benefit Flávio Bolsonaro, a Trump-aligned pre-candidate for president. They accuse the Trump administration of using the tariffs to blackmail Brazil in favor of Bolsonaro’s electoral interests, linking the decision to issues like Pix, deforestation, and judicial rulings against big techs, while attempting to divert attention from the Master Case and Flávio’s ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: Lula x Flávio: levantamento mostra vencedor nas redes após tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: A study by Ativaweb DataLab for VEJA reveals that in the first 24 hours after the U.S. imposed tariffs on Brazilian products, Lula strengthened his image on social media as a defender of national sovereignty and Pix, while Flávio Bolsonaro suffered the greatest reputational damage, driven by the spread of the term 'TariFlávio'. The episode generated 21.45 million mentions and interactions, shifting the debate from economics to a political narrative over who should bear responsibility for the crisis, with strong support for the Reciprocity Law and limited traction for the opposition's 'Faz o L' narrative.

item.title: Petição ao STF pede investigação sobre “clones” de Vini Jr e Bill Gates
item.description: Lawyer Kelmo Martins Bandeira filed a petition with the STF requesting a Federal Police investigation into an alleged international organization called '666' or 'Babylon' that supposedly clones and replaces public figures such as Vini Jr, Bill Gates, and Mark Zuckerberg, without presenting any scientific evidence. The petition also names Lula, Bolsonaro, Pope Leo XIV, and Leonardo DiCaprio as defendants, seeking monthly indemnities ranging from R$2,000 to R$35,000 for celebrities and percentage-based payments on the net revenue of companies like Meta, Microsoft, and Ambev. The action lacks legal grounding and may be immediately dismissed as absurd, with the plaintiff potentially facing fines for bad-faith litigation.

item.title: A apresentação de Ratinho Junior a Caiado durante visita ao Paraná
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado visited Paraná, where he was received by Governor Ratinho Junior to learn about part of the state's new public security fleet. The presentation included Canadian-made Roshel tactical armored vehicles, RAM 3500 Longhorn pickup trucks, and new BMW motorcycles for the Military Police, all incorporated this year for high-complexity operations.

item.title: Ministro estima impacto de US$ 7,4 bilhões nas exportações aos EUA
item.description: Brazil's Minister of Development, Industry, Commerce and Services, Márcio Elias Rosa, estimated that the new 25% U.S. tariff will impact US$7.4 billion in Brazilian exports, equivalent to about 18% of sales to the United States, based on 2024 data. He emphasized that the Lula government prioritizes support for affected sectors — including wood, machinery, electrical equipment, furniture, ceramics, footwear, and sugar — and noted that 74% of the 2,400 Brazilian companies exporting to the U.S. have already begun diversifying markets, reducing U.S. share in Brazil’s exports from 12.1% to 9.4%.

item.title: Eleições: TSE assina acordo contra clonagem de voz e proteção de dados
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) signed agreements with major digital platforms and AI companies to combat disinformation and unauthorized voice cloning in the 2026 elections. The agreement includes the use of ElevenLabs' No-Go Voices technology to protect the voices of public figures such as presidential candidates, state governors, and STF ministers, with an official channel to designate which voices should be protected. Google renewed its MoU with the TSE, originally established in 2014, reinforcing its commitment to providing quality information.

item.title: Trump tem duas guerras em curso: uma contra o Irã, outra contra o Brasil, diz ex-embaixador nos EUA
item.description: Former Brazilian ambassador Roberto Abdenur claims Donald Trump is waging two wars: a military one against Iran and a political and economic one against Brazil, citing the imposition of 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods and the breakdown of diplomatic dialogue. He argues Brazil has become a preferential target of U.S. commercial aggression, despite maintaining a $424 billion trade surplus with the U.S. over the last 15 years. Abdenur describes the current international order as a lawless 'barbarism' that has ended the post-WWII era of relative peace and prosperity.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio reconhece ganho eleitoral de Lula com tarifaço e aposta em passar ônus para o PT
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro acknowledge that the new U.S. tariff on Brazil initially benefits Lula, who is trying to blame the opposition. However, they believe the impact will be smaller and more reversible than Trump’s 2025 tariff, and plan to shift the economic burden onto the PT.

item.title: Justiça Eleitoral fornecerá transporte a eleitores com mobilidade reduzida
item.description: The Electoral Justice will launch the 'Your Vote Matters' program in the 2026 elections, providing free transportation for voters with reduced mobility or from historically vulnerable groups, including Indigenous peoples, quilombola communities, and rural residents. Coordinated nationally by the TSE and implemented locally by the TREs, the service allows requests in person or online by September 14, requiring self-declaration or simple documentation, with logistical partnerships established at no additional cost.

item.title: “Já tinha visto essa foto há mais de um mês”, diz Valdemar
item.description: PL party president Valdemar Costa Neto stated he had seen over a month ago the photo showing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro alongside Luiz Phillipi Machado de Moraes Mourão, known as Sicário. He downplayed the image's significance, saying politicians often appear in photos and that Flávio is just a politician like any other.

item.title: Em reação a tarifaço dos EUA, governo amplia ajuda a empresas e estuda retaliação, dizem ministros
item.description: The Brazilian government announced an expansion of the Brasil Soberano program to support companies affected by the new 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian exports, which impacts approximately 18% of Brazil’s sales to the United States. Ministers also confirmed they are studying retaliatory measures under the Economic Reciprocity Law, with open meetings scheduled with President Lula to define actions in response to what they view as a violation of international trade rules.

item.title: Justiça Eleitoral manda derrubar 21 postagens contra Tarcísio e multa coordenador da pré-campanha de Haddad por vídeo com Chucky
item.description: Brazil's Electoral Justice ordered the removal of 21 posts against Tarcísio de Freitas for premature negative campaigning and false information, including an AI-generated video linking his image to the Chucky character. Fernando Haddad’s pre-campaign coordinator, Emídio de Souza, was fined R$10,000 and barred from republishing the content. The actions were filed by the Republicanos party against PT lawmakers and anonymous social media profiles.

item.title: Tarifaço de Trump é interferência externa indevida, diz ministro da Fazenda
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan labeled the U.S. tariff increase as an improper external interference with political motives, claiming it aims to pressure Brazil and its workers. He stated the government has ready protective mechanisms for businesses and will strengthen the Brazil Sovereign Plan to support affected sectors, while noting the potential for retaliation under the recently approved reciprocity law. Durigan also linked the tariff to political interests of the Bolsonaro family, referencing Flávio Bolsonaro’s recent trip to the U.S. as an attempt to gain electoral advantage from the situation.

item.title: Direção nacional do PT já trata candidatura de Patrus Ananias em Minas como certa, mas aguarda encontro com Lula
item.description: The national leadership of the Workers' Party (PT) already treats Patrus Ananias' candidacy for governor of Minas Gerais as certain, awaiting only a meeting with President Lula to confirm the nomination. Patrus emerged as the choice after other candidates, such as Marília Campos and Rodrigo Pacheco, declined, and is seen as a unifying figure due to his background as former mayor of Belo Horizonte and minister in the Lula and Dilma governments.

item.title: Após tarifaço, Haddad diz que Tarcísio foi ingênuo ao apoiar Trump
item.description: Fernando Haddad, the PT’s pre-candidate for governor of São Paulo, criticized Governor Tarcísio de Freitas for supporting the U.S. government, calling his stance naive after the U.S. imposed a 25% tariff on Brazilian exports. Haddad said São Paulo is the most affected state and that Tarcísio’s support for Trump undermines the 200-year-old partnership between Brazil and the U.S., urging the governor to reassess and self-criticize his position.

item.title: PIX: Galípolo defende meio de pagamento alvo de contestação dos EUA; 'gratuito', 'seguro' e 'instantâneo'
item.description: Central Bank President Gabriel Galípolo defended PIX as a free, secure, and instant payment method during a press conference, emphasizing its role in financial inclusion. His remarks came in response to a U.S. trade investigation accusing Brazil of practices that burden trade, citing PIX as an example. Galípolo stressed that PIX reduces reliance on checks and cash and that the BC is working to expand technical cooperation with other central banks to promote PIX globally.

item.title: O saldo nas redes para Lula e Flávio após o novo tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: An Agora Comunicação e Public Affairs analysis revealed that the new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products generated more negative social media mentions for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (280,000) than for President Lula (213,000), despite nearly identical negative sentiment levels (68.6% vs. 68.0%). Criticism of Flávio is dispersed across multiple actors, including Lula and allies, while his defense is largely self-generated, making it easier to caricature. The report highlights greater risk for Flávio due to his family’s ties to Donald Trump, but warns Lula also faces electoral limits in defending national sovereignty amid the tariffs.

item.title: Casado: Candidatura de Flávio é questionada por apoiadores após tarifaço
item.description: The 25% tariff imposed by the United States on Brazilian products is directly impacting Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, causing allies to question the viability of his candidacy, according to Letícia Casado on UOL News.

item.title: Ex-aliado cobra “exame toxicológico” de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Former federal deputy Julian Lemos, ex-coordinator of Jair Bolsonaro’s 2018 campaign in Paraíba, challenged Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to take a toxicology test and publish the results, implying drug use. The post on X (formerly Twitter) sparked controversy among Bolsonaro allies.

item.title: Governo e oposição trocam críticas após novas tarifas dos EUA
item.description: The Brazilian government and its allies accused the United States of imposing a 25% tariff on Brazilian exports as retaliation for alleged unfair trade practices, linking the measure to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and the Trump administration. The opposition criticized Lula’s foreign policy as ideologically driven and ineffective, claiming it provoked the U.S. response. Both sides announced countermeasures, with the government pledging to use the Reciprocity Law and WTO instruments to defend national interests.

item.title: Renan Santos atribui cancelamento de show à "sabotagem da esquerda"
item.description: Renan Santos, a presidential pré-candidate for the Missão party and lead singer of the band Limão Rosa, blamed the cancellation of a show at Audio Rebel in Botafogo (RJ) on a "sabotage" by the left, after the venue stated it did not want to risk associating its brand with a political figure in pre-campaign. Santos criticized the public’s reaction and claimed the cancellation resulted from social media pressure, insisting his band only sings about existential and relationship themes, not politics.
